chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who doubted, so he did not know whether he had performed one prostration or two. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should prostrate until he is convinced that they are two prostrations.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they are unsure whether they performed one or two prostrations in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in cases of doubt regarding the number of prostrations, instructing the worshipper to continue until certainty is achieved. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for resolving ambiguity through active verification rather than assuming the minimum, ensuring the prayer's validity through *istiqanah*. This ruling reflects the broader Shia methodology of prioritizing certainty over conjecture in ritual acts.
